As a human, a slightly hunched over average looking dude with straw like hair and a sunken face. A straight up 4/10 kind of guy.

As a beaver he is considered a handsome fellow. Rigid, reliable, but kind of unpersonable. 7/10.

background.label: Background
background.value:
Old Wild You spent a lifetime — longer than most civilizations endure — trapped in an animal form. You are more beast than person, and the wild has seeped into your bones.


You may Shapeshift into any creature you have encountered, not only your Attuned Creatures. When shifted into a non-attuned form, your Instinct is always that of your true form, and you carry a visible physical tell of your true nature.

biography.label: Biography
biography.value:
In the days before Beaconhold's rise to a larger empire, Castor was a normal little peasant who did his daily work in his family's generational land in what would be known as the Ashen Vale. But some day, for reasons beyond his knowing, he was "cursed" to take the form of a beaver.

But not just a beaver, a seemingly immortal beaver. For hundreds of years he plied his trade as a beaver with some level of fulfillment, but eventually found himself curious about the world he could reach and his long lived life. Living a solitary life as a human he had no children to check in on, he still had an attachment to his home and family, but he would regularly take journeys to see what parts of the world a modest beaver could.

Upon returning home from one of these excursions he found someone with his familiar pointed ear features resettling the Ashen Vale with some success. Sure of the kinship between them (and cozy in his beaver homeland) he began to shadow the aged "lord". This "lord" noticed the beaver and became curious in kind of the unique creature.

This in combination with Garland's own research on the strange magic in the Vale resulted in a temporary lifting of the curse that forced him to be a beaver. Now he finds himself with the ability to change between animal forms, though his heart still yearns for the dams and closed lips behind his teeth.

system.description:
When you assist one of your companions in an act, you grant them Advantage to any rolls made as part of it, but you are both fully affected by any costs or consequences.

Multiple people can Cooperate with the same person at once, that person simply gains additional Advantage per person. You can Cooperate before a Move's roll is made, but not after.

When you use favor, payment, promises, or threats to get someone to do something, say what you want them to do (or not to do) and roll+CHA. If they Favor you, you may use up their Favor to gain Advantage on the roll.

If they are a PC, on a 10+ both below occur, on a 7-9 choose one below, and on a 6- they instead can immediately ask you two questions as if they Scrutinized you.
• If they do it, you will Favor them.
• If they don't do it, they have Disadvantage Forward and you no longer Favor them.

success.label: Success!
success.value: If they are an NPC, they'll do what you want.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: If they are an NPC, they'll only do it if you do something for them in return or Favor them afterwards, the GM will say which.

system.description: When you attack a clear target from afar, roll+DEX.

success.label: Success!
success.value: Your clean hit inflicts a condition.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: You inflict a condition but are either put in a dangerous position or gain Disadvantage Forward, your choice.

system.description:
When you study someone during an intimate or prying conversation with them, roll+WIS.

Gain +1 Insight if they Favor you, even on a 6-.

During this conversation you can spend Insight 1-for-1 to ask their player (including the GM) any question about this person's thoughts, feelings, or motivations and they must answer truthfully.

Example questions:
• How might I get you to ___?
• How do you feel about ___?
• How can I gain your Favor?
• What is your goal?

success.label: Success!
success.value: Gain 2 Insight.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: Gain 1 Insight.

system.description:
When you closely investigate a charged situation, ask the GM one question about it and roll+WIS.

You and your allies roll with Advantage when first acting on this information.

Example questions:
• Who/what else is hidden?
• How can I gain the upper hand?
• What would happen here if I ___?
• Who is really in control here?

success.label: Success!
success.value: The GM answers your question and related followup questions truthfully.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: The GM answers your question truthfully.

system.description:
When you consider what you know about a subject, ask the GM one question about it, say how you might know the answer, and roll+INT.

You and your allies have Advantage when first acting on this information.

Example questions:
• Where is ___ located?
• What could have caused ___?
• What might be the best way to ___?
• What have I heard or read about this person/creature?

success.label: Success!
success.value: The GM will tell you the detailed, useful truth.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: They will tell you a vague, twisted, or incomplete truth.

system.description: When you openly fight an enemy up close, roll+STR.

success.label: Success!
success.value:
You trade blows, but choose one:
• Avoid or withstand their attack
• Inflict an extra condition
• Take something from them

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: You and your enemy trade blows, usually inflicting a condition on each other.

system.description:
When you spend time resting as a group, whether it's taking a short break, sleeping overnight, or relaxing for weeks, the GM advances the Ominous Forces. Then, if anyone has 5 or more XP, they Level Up. If you have enough XP, you can Level Up multiple times at once.

When you've finished resting and resume adventuring, remove all your conditions and refresh your Armor.

When you act despite an imminent threat or obstacle, say how you do it. Then roll...

• +STR if you endure or power through it.
• +DEX if you act with speed or finesse.
• +INT if you employ quick or out-of-the-box thinking.
• +WIS if you rely on mental fortitude or sharp senses.
• +CHA if you use charm, intrigue, or social grace.

success.label: Success!
success.value: The threat doesn't come to bear.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: It only abates if you make a costly sacrifice or ugly choice, the GM will tell you what.

system.description: When you put all of your effort into one act, roll with Advantage. Then after the roll, you take a condition from the strain, which ignores Armor.

When you have 5 or more XP after Settling In, reduce your XP by 5, increase your Level by 1, and choose one benefit below:

You can always take these options:
• Increase a stat of your choice from +0 to +1.
• Take an Advanced Move from your playbook.
• Acquire an Asset (see Page 26).
• Remove a Locked condition (see Crumble).
• Change Playbooks (see Page 81).

You can take these options only once each:
• Increase a stat of your choice from +1 to +2.
• Increase a stat of your choice from +1 to +2.
• Take a Starting or Advanced Move from another playbook.
• Take a Starting or Advanced Move from another playbook.

Once you reach Level 10 you can also always take these options:
• Take an Advanced Move (Level 10+) from your playbook.
• Increase a stat of your choice from +2 to +3.
• Retire to safety and cease your adventuring.

At the end of each session, answer the following questions as a group:

• Did we discover something new and important about the world or characters?
• Did we newly visit or significantly alter a memorable location?
• Did we overcome a notable obstacle, enemy, or challenge?

For each "yes" answer, everyone marks 1 XP.

Lastly, gain 1 XP if you accomplished your Drive.

When you return after being away for a session or more, and explain your absence, say what happened and roll...

• +STR if you fought an enemy or escaped captivity.
• +DEX if you did something covert or illicit.
• +INT if you learned obscure or ancient knowledge, or invented something.
• +WIS if you discovered a scandalous secret, went on a long journey or retreat, or had a spiritual encounter.
• +CHA if you made an ally, integrated with a group or culture, or bought something interesting.

success.label: Success!
success.value: Your adventure was prosperous - gain Advantage Forward and 2 XP.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: Your adventure was eventful - gain 2 XP, but the GM will tell you one or two unintended consequences.

failure.label: Miss...
failure.value: Your adventure was perilous - gain 1 XP and the GM will say what trouble has followed you back to the entire group.

system.description: When you Compel someone open to bribes, offering 1 Wealth gives you Advantage, and offering 2 Wealth lets you automatically succeed as if you had rolled a 10+.
When you declare you know an NPC who could help and go looking for them, roll+CHA. If you also declare that you Favor them, gain Advantage on the roll.

success.label: Success!
success.value: You easily find them and they're willing to help.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value:
They might help you, but the GM will choose one:
• They have a grudge against you or aren't entirely willing to trust you.
• They're already caught up in some trouble.
• They're far off, hiding, trapped, or hard to find.

system.description:
When you mark your last condition (other than Armor), your life is untenable.

When your life is untenable, from conditions or otherwise, you're out of the action for a while. Say how and choose one from the list below:

• Lock a condition of your choice. It can't be removed except through a Level Up. You still gain XP from rolling with it.
• Change to a new Playbook (see Page 81)
• Die

If you're not dead, remove all conditions that aren't Locked. The GM will advance the Ominous Forces and say when you're back in the action.
When you have a change of heart, say what is behind it and write a new Drive.
When you venture out from safety in lengthy pursuit of a quarry, roll+Nothing, with Advantage if you already know your quarry's location.

success.label: Success!
success.value:
Choose one.
• You are exhausted or distracted. All traveling PCs take a condition from fatigue.
• You are noticed, by your quarry or by someone else, and they act accordingly.
• You are impeded. A significant obstacle stands between you and your quarry.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value:
Choose two.
• You are exhausted or distracted. All traveling PCs take a condition from fatigue.
• You are noticed, by your quarry or by someone else, and they act accordingly.
• You are impeded. A significant obstacle stands between you and your quarry.

failure.label: Miss...
failure.value:
All three.
• You are exhausted or distracted. All traveling PCs take a condition from fatigue.
• You are noticed, by your quarry or by someone else, and they act accordingly.
• You are impeded. A significant obstacle stands between you and your quarry.

system.description: When you Examine by gathering rumors and information from others, you may spend 1 Wealth to roll with Advantage.

You are one with the wild places of the world. The spirits of nature speak to you, and you can take their forms. Civilization is a thin veneer over the primal world, and you walk the boundary between both.
Starting Move. You can speak with animals and Scrutinize and Compel them. You also don't require food or drink.
Attunement When you spend meaningful time observing, interacting with, or embodying a creature, you may attempt to attune with it. Roll+WIS.

success.label: Success!
success.value: Name the creature and choose its Instinct. Your physical tell fades in this form.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value:
Choose one:

  • A trace of your true form's Instinct bleeds into the new attunement.

  • Your physical tell persists in this form despite the attunement.

  • Creatures of this species sense you as an outsider — they react to you with suspicion, unease, or hostility.

system.description: Starting Move. When you spend some time in a place, connecting with nearby creatures and spirits, roll+WIS. You will be granted a vision of significance to you, your allies, or the spirits around you, the GM will describe it.

success.label: Success!
success.value: The vision will be clear and helpful.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: The vision is unclear and murky.

system.description:
Starting Move. When you call upon the wilds to change your shape, choose one of your Attuned Creatures to change into and roll+WIS.

While in an animal shape, you gain any innate abilities and weaknesses of the form: claws, wings, gills, etc. You also gain the Instinct of your new form. This primal urge is something innate to each creature and becomes a part of you while you are shapeshifted.

You don't need to Shapeshift to change back into your normal shape, though you may need to Resist Instinct.

success.label: Success!
success.value: You transform quickly and without issue.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: You still transform, but you draw unwanted attention or trouble.

system.description: Starting Move. When you try to change shape without having fulfilled your Instinct, roll+WIS.

success.label: Success!
success.value: You succeed and are now able to transform. If you're changing back to normal, you do so. If you're changing into another creature, roll to Shapeshift.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: You succeed, but won't be able to transform back into your previous form until you reattune with it by fulfilling its Instinct.

system.choices: Beaver: Reshape the world around me in a beaver-like way: Dam it up, build a pleasing structure, make it safer for your kin

Wears a faded yellow scarf, finely woven, bearing the symbols of the [[Middle Kingdoms]] — the confederacy of kingdoms that formed after the [[Imperium Lucis Aeternae]] fell.

The weave occasionally reveals a broken sunburst ring — an old royal symbol of a fallen line of kings — that only becomes visible when the fabric moves just right.

Traveling Artist

You traversed the land in pursuit of inspiration, and earned your keep practicing and promoting your art wherever you went.

When you Perform, gain +1 Awe even on a 6-. Additionally, you have 4 Art for Expressive Conflict instead of 3.

Starting Stats: +2 CHA, +1 DEX

Equipment: Adventuring Gear (4 Uses)

biography.label: Biography
biography.value:
Edric was born in a small village along the [[Eastern Rivers]] — a hamlet on the edge of the kingdom where tax collectors don't bother going.

His mother had an "angelic voice" which Edric inherited.

His father is unknown — his mother would never speak of him.

He has wandered far from home and doesn't really know his mother anymore.

He apprenticed with the town merchant who worked with traveling traders.

He took to the life of a wandering trader, paying his way by telling stories and singing songs at taverns.

He also trades in "rare and curious goods" — some of which may not be exactly what he claims they are.

Edric is a lean man with a calm, steady presence and an unmistakable voice that carries without effort.

He dresses like someone who has traveled long roads and slept in good and bad rooms alike.

He moves with a calm, steady grace and never seems rushed, even when others expect him to be.

Starting Move. You wield renowned artistic skill (music, writing, painting, etc.), which can do more than just capture hearts and minds. Choose two expressions that you know:

• Heal yourself or an ally of 1 condition.
• Distract, stun, or immobilize a foe.

You have 3 Art. When you Settle In, reset your Art to this number. When you invoke your artistry, you may spend 1 Art and unleash one known expression.

Starting Move. When you first encounter someone or something that you've heard tales, songs, or legends about (your call), tell the GM something interesting you've heard about it. The GM will tell you what else you've heard that complicates things.

Starting Move. When you practice or display your chosen art before an intelligent audience, roll+CHA.

During or shortly after your performance, you can spend each Awe to name an NPC in the audience and choose one:
• This person must speak with me.
• This person must give me a gift.
• This person Favors me.

system.description: You are the storyteller, the musician, the artist, the performer, the muse. Your art shapes the hearts and minds of all who witness it. You are the chronicler of this group's great adventure - and possibly its greatest hero.

Be it amongst street urchins, traveling merchants, or wealthy nobles, you know people and people know you.

When you spread the word about something unusual you want or need, roll+CHA.

success.label: Success!
success.value: someone has it, just for you.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: you’ll have to settle for something close, or it comes with strings attached, your choice.

system.description: When you insult, injure, or disappoint someone who Favors you, they no longer do.

• Heal them of one condition; describe how you do so.
• Gain Advantage Forward to aid them or accomplish something for them.

• Gain 1 XP
• You no longer Favor them
• They Favor you
• You get to ask them two questions as if you Scrutinized them

Veteran

Whether on the front lines of a battle or the back roads of a quiet village, you’ve learned to always trust your gut.

When you get a bad feeling about an upcoming situation (your call), ask the GM how to avoid or prepare for it and they will give you one piece of advice.

If you follow it, gain +1 Momentum.

biography.label: Biography
biography.value:
Max armor is 3 (2 from heavy armor, 1 from second harvest)

XP: xxxx

Garland, just Garland, is a very old man entering his third act. He served as a soldier in his youth, marching with drum and fife in hand as a child, and retired to a barren plot of land earned as spoils of war.

There he carved out a farm and family, eventually forced to sell and rent out parcels of his land over time until he found himself known locally as Garland yn Greenholt upon the Ashen Vale, an accidental lord in practice though he would never accept the title.

While preparing a well-hidden field for pasture, he discovered a set of standing stones known variously as the Shepherds Teeth and the Witchstones, which he studied carefully over the years (guarding the secret of their location carefully once he learned the power that dwelt there).

With his wife long gone (and, in fact, several of his children having passed as well), and tired of being called lord, he left the farm in the hands of the ever-growing clan he begat, and set off with fife and drum in hand.

system.description:
When you assist one of your companions in an act, you grant them Advantage to any rolls made as part of it, but you are both fully affected by any costs or consequences.

Multiple people can Cooperate with the same person at once, that person simply gains additional Advantage per person. You can Cooperate before a Move's roll is made, but not after.

When you use favor, payment, promises, or threats to get someone to do something, say what you want them to do (or not to do) and roll+CHA. If they Favor you, you may use up their Favor to gain Advantage on the roll.

If they are a PC, on a 10+ both below occur, on a 7-9 choose one below, and on a 6- they instead can immediately ask you two questions as if they Scrutinized you.
• If they do it, you will Favor them.
• If they don't do it, they have Disadvantage Forward and you no longer Favor them.

success.label: Success!
success.value: If they are an NPC, they'll do what you want.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: If they are an NPC, they'll only do it if you do something for them in return or Favor them afterwards, the GM will say which.

system.description: When you attack a clear target from afar, roll+DEX.

success.label: Success!
success.value: Your clean hit inflicts a condition.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: You inflict a condition but are either put in a dangerous position or gain Disadvantage Forward, your choice.

system.description:
When you study someone during an intimate or prying conversation with them, roll+WIS.

Gain +1 Insight if they Favor you, even on a 6-.

During this conversation you can spend Insight 1-for-1 to ask their player (including the GM) any question about this person's thoughts, feelings, or motivations and they must answer truthfully.

Example questions:
• How might I get you to ___?
• How do you feel about ___?
• How can I gain your Favor?
• What is your goal?

success.label: Success!
success.value: Gain 2 Insight.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: Gain 1 Insight.

system.description:
When you closely investigate a charged situation, ask the GM one question about it and roll+WIS.

You and your allies roll with Advantage when first acting on this information.

Example questions:
• Who/what else is hidden?
• How can I gain the upper hand?
• What would happen here if I ___?
• Who is really in control here?

success.label: Success!
success.value: The GM answers your question and related followup questions truthfully.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: The GM answers your question truthfully.

system.description:
When you consider what you know about a subject, ask the GM one question about it, say how you might know the answer, and roll+INT.

You and your allies have Advantage when first acting on this information.

Example questions:
• Where is ___ located?
• What could have caused ___?
• What might be the best way to ___?
• What have I heard or read about this person/creature?

success.label: Success!
success.value: The GM will tell you the detailed, useful truth.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: They will tell you a vague, twisted, or incomplete truth.

success.label: Success!
success.value:

• Avoid or withstand their attack
• Inflict an extra condition
• Take something from them

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: You and your enemy trade blows, usually inflicting a condition on each other.

system.description:
When you spend time resting as a group, whether it's taking a short break, sleeping overnight, or relaxing for weeks, the GM advances the Ominous Forces. Then, if anyone has 5 or more XP, they Level Up. If you have enough XP, you can Level Up multiple times at once.

When you've finished resting and resume adventuring, remove all your conditions and refresh your Armor.

When you act despite an imminent threat or obstacle, say how you do it. Then roll...

• +STR if you endure or power through it.
• +DEX if you act with speed or finesse.
• +INT if you employ quick or out-of-the-box thinking.
• +WIS if you rely on mental fortitude or sharp senses.
• +CHA if you use charm, intrigue, or social grace.

success.label: Success!
success.value: The threat doesn't come to bear.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: It only abates if you make a costly sacrifice or ugly choice, the GM will tell you what.

system.description: When you put all of your effort into one act, roll with Advantage. Then after the roll, you take a condition from the strain, which ignores Armor.

When you have 5 or more XP after Settling In, reduce your XP by 5, increase your Level by 1, and choose one benefit below:

You can always take these options:
• Increase a stat of your choice from +0 to +1.
• Take an Advanced Move from your playbook.
• Acquire an Asset (see Page 26).
• Remove a Locked condition (see Crumble).
• Change Playbooks (see Page 81).

You can take these options only once each:
• Increase a stat of your choice from +1 to +2.
• Increase a stat of your choice from +1 to +2.
• Take a Starting or Advanced Move from another playbook.
• Take a Starting or Advanced Move from another playbook.

Once you reach Level 10 you can also always take these options:
• Take an Advanced Move (Level 10+) from your playbook.
• Increase a stat of your choice from +2 to +3.
• Retire to safety and cease your adventuring.

At the end of each session, answer the following questions as a group:

• Did we discover something new and important about the world or characters?
• Did we newly visit or significantly alter a memorable location?
• Did we overcome a notable obstacle, enemy, or challenge?

For each "yes" answer, everyone marks 1 XP.

Lastly, gain 1 XP if you accomplished your Drive.

When you return after being away for a session or more, and explain your absence, say what happened and roll...

• +STR if you fought an enemy or escaped captivity.
• +DEX if you did something covert or illicit.
• +INT if you learned obscure or ancient knowledge, or invented something.
• +WIS if you discovered a scandalous secret, went on a long journey or retreat, or had a spiritual encounter.
• +CHA if you made an ally, integrated with a group or culture, or bought something interesting.

When you declare you know an NPC who could help and go looking for them, roll+CHA. If you also declare that you Favor them, gain Advantage on the roll.

success.label: Success!
success.value: You easily find them and they're willing to help.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value:
They might help you, but the GM will choose one:
• They have a grudge against you or aren't entirely willing to trust you.
• They're already caught up in some trouble.
• They're far off, hiding, trapped, or hard to find.

system.description:
When you mark your last condition (other than Armor), your life is untenable.

When your life is untenable, from conditions or otherwise, you're out of the action for a while. Say how and choose one from the list below:

• Lock a condition of your choice. It can't be removed except through a Level Up. You still gain XP from rolling with it.
• Change to a new Playbook (see Page 81)
• Die

If you're not dead, remove all conditions that aren't Locked. The GM will advance the Ominous Forces and say when you're back in the action.
When you have a change of heart, say what is behind it and write a new Drive.
When you venture out from safety in lengthy pursuit of a quarry, roll+Nothing, with Advantage if you already know your quarry's location.

success.label: Success!
success.value:
Choose one.
• You are exhausted or distracted. All traveling PCs take a condition from fatigue.
• You are noticed, by your quarry or by someone else, and they act accordingly.
• You are impeded. A significant obstacle stands between you and your quarry.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value:
Choose two.
• You are exhausted or distracted. All traveling PCs take a condition from fatigue.
• You are noticed, by your quarry or by someone else, and they act accordingly.
• You are impeded. A significant obstacle stands between you and your quarry.

failure.label: Miss...
failure.value:
All three.

• You are noticed, by your quarry or by someone else, and they act accordingly.

You are a warrior, born and bred for battle. Where others see obstacles, you see opportunities to test your skill. Your weapon is an extension of your will, and your will is iron.

Garland's signature weapon, Second Harvest, once called Halcyrax, the Gilded Ruin, once a plowshare, now again a sword.

  • Ignores armor

  • Provides +1 armor
Garland's armor is as old as he is, dusty and rusty and hidden away for centuries, dented and damaged from years of battle, and hidden by his tattered riding cloak.
Concealed throwing knives. Too many to count.
A defensive shield that adds to your existing Armor.

These might be poultices to heal wounds, herbal supplements to calm nerves, or similar remedies. When you take a few minutes to prepare and use Medicine, mark off a use and heal 2 conditions or another affliction on yourself or someone else.
Starting Move. When you Compel with threats of violence, roll with Advantage.

Starting Move. When you unleash your magical talents, choose a Spell you know and roll+SPELL.

You start with 2 Spells known. When you Level Up, you can choose to Learn a New Spell instead of another benefit.

SPELL is determined by your Background (INT for Scholar, WIS for Seer, CHA for Sorceror).

success.label: Success!
success.value: You successfully evoke the Spell and its effects come to pass.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value:
The Spell is still successful but choose one consequence:
• The Spell's Risk manifests as well.
• The Spell's magic drains you. You take -1 Ongoing to Evoke Spells until you next Settle In.
• Using it puts you in danger or draws unwanted attention, the GM will say how.

system.description: Starting Move. You can easily invoke minor magical effects without issue. Slowly moving small objects, creating minor obvious illusions, generating mild heat and sources of light, and other similar feats are all easily within your power without Evoking a Spell or performing a Ritual.

Ongoing. Name one specific source of harm, such as burning, cutting, lightning, poisonous gas, or mundane projectiles; for as long as this Spell is Ongoing, you are immune to harm from that source (as well as any secondary effects; choking smoke, hypothermia, etc.).

Risk: You gain +2 Armor against it but are not immune.
Greater: Nearby allies are equally protected.
Starting Move. You don't wield an ordinary weapon, but instead have an especially powerful or unusual one. See the Signature Weapon asset for details on creating it.

Starting Move. You perfectly understand the back and forth rhythm of a fight. When you suffer or inflict harm as part of a fight (even if it's absorbed with Armor), gain 1 Momentum. Anytime during a fight, you may spend the amount of Momentum in brackets for the following:

• (3) Restore 1 of your Armor
• (3) Inflict an extra condition on an attack
• (2) Gain Advantage Forward to Engage or Let Fly

You can have a maximum of 5 Momentum. When you Settle In, reset Momentum to 0.

You or an ally you touch becomes invisible for the scene or until they attack.

Risk: Either one creature can still see them clear as day, or anyone perceptive enough might notice a shimmer; the GM will say which.
Greater: The effect is Ongoing and persists after attacking. It still only lasts for the scene.

biography.label: Biography
biography.value:
Sir Roderic, was raised by the church as a war orphan. Originally Roderic wanted to be a Cleric to heal all the people of the world. He grew up in the orphanage and helped the clerics heal and eventually was accepted into the Church academy.

After spending a year there he finally realized that he did not have enough talent for healing. However, he did have talent, a talent for protecting the weak and fighting evil and repression. So he transferred from the healing order to the church's war college.

Roderick then spent years on the battlefields spreading the church's doctrine and eliminating evil. On his last campaign, tragedy struck and he lost his entire regiment. He blamed himself for not being able to defend his brothers. This caused Rodrick to realize that he needed to take a sabbatical where he could focus on defending and healing those in need. Currently a Knight-Errant of the Redeemer's of Light

You are a champion of righteousness, bound by sacred virtues. Your strength comes not just from your arm, but from your unwavering commitment to justice and your devout principles. Where corruption festers, you are the cleansing flame.
Sharp
Reliable
Polished
Ruby head of Lucifer surrounded by beams of golden light
Slow
Slow

Starting Move. You adhere to a strict moral code that grants you power beyond that wielded by normal folk. Each virtue has a vow that must be kept and a boon it grants you. Choose two now:

• Courage: Refuse to let those who have power abuse it. While you physically stand in defense of another, they will not be targeted or harmed.
• Honor: Never harm the helpless or unaware. When you Decree an enemy to surrender or repent, you can treat a 6- as a 7-9.
• Justice: Suffer not a crime unpunished. When you question a captive or friendly individual, you know if they're lying.
• Loyalty: Remain true to your word and to your allies. Gain +1 Armor. When an ally Cooperates with you, you can share your Armor with them against conditions suffered from Cooperation.
• Mercy: Let no innocent creature suffer unaided in your presence. When you heal someone else, you are also healed of one condition.
• Purity: Abstain from mortal pleasures and finery. You are immune to all maladies, such as poisons, diseases, and curses.
Starting Move. When you demand an NPC follow your order, roll+CHA.

success.label: Success!
success.value:
Choose two, then they flee, attack, or obey you:
• If they do anything other than obey you, gain Advantage Forward against them.
• They reveal a piece of relevant information to you (unwittingly or otherwise).
• They cannot flee.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: Choose one, then they flee, attack, or obey you.

system.description: Starting Move. When you break one of the vows of your Devout Virtues, depending on the severity of your actions, you may lose access to that virtue and its associated benefits until you atone for your misdeeds. The GM will tell you what you must do.
Starting Move. Ignore the Clumsy tag on armor you wear.

Starting Move. When you treat someone with Supplies or Medicine, choose one additional effect:
• It ignores the Slow tag, taking a few moments rather than minutes.
• Heal them of an additional Condition.
• The patient gains Advantage Forward (PCs only).

• When you Examine a place or situation, you may also ask "what sin or wrongdoing has occurred or is occurring here?" and the GM will answer honestly, even on a 6-.

  • When you Scrutinize a person, you may also ask "what guilt or transgression weighs on them?" and the GM will answer honestly, even on a 6-.

  • When you use either move, it is because you sense that something is morally wrong — the GM should treat your use of these moves as a signal that sin is present, even if you don't yet know what it is.

When you Connect with a fellow member of your organization, you may choose to Favor them to gain Advantage on your roll.

The Light (the Luciferian church). He is a knight-errant of the Redeemers of Light, reporting to a superior in the church hierarchy. He carries the authority and recognition of a paladin — soldiers have deferred to his rank, and the church's institutional weight backs his actions. This formalizes the social standing and authority he's already exercised in play (e.g., invoking his authority to force the Aureate soldiers to release Jimmy).

When you navigate an imminent environmental danger (ongoing trap, rockslide, wildfire, etc.), use the Chase Moves as normal but with the following changes:

• When you Gain the Edge using knowledge or out-of-the-box thinking, roll+INT.
• If the environment's side loses the chase, it may not spend Edge to Learn something of another side, but may spend Edge to inflict 1 Condition on all characters on another side, including PCs.
• Every PC on the losing side Crumbles.

When you try to get ahead in a chase, say how much Edge you risk (1 to 3), and roll...

• +STR if you create or destroy obstacles.
• +DEX if you sprint, hide or maneuver.
• +INT if you distract or misdirect.
• +WIS if you watch or listen.
• +CHA if you disguise or provoke.

Then, unless a side has 3 or more Edge, the chase continues and the GM describes what happens next.

success.label: Success!
success.value: Your side gains that Edge.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value: Your side and an opposing side both gain that Edge. If there are multiple opposing sides, you choose which one gains it.

failure.label: Miss...
failure.value: An opposing side gains that Edge, the GM will say which.

system.description:
When any side in a chase has 3 or more Edge, the chase comes to an end. Whoever has the most Edge succeeds in escaping or catching their quarry. If multiple sides tie for the most Edge, the side with the most PCs wins (just barely). If that is also tied, then the PC that last Gained the Edge chooses one side to win, with the other tying sides gaining +1 Edge for the purposes of spending it below.

Losing sides can spend their Edge 1-for-1 to:
• Learn something about another party (where they will go, who leads them, how to escape them now, etc.)
• Have the chase end somewhere advantageous for them (reinforcements, a trap or lair, an intervening third party, etc.)
• Grant Advantage Forward to all PCs on their side.
• Inflict Disadvantage Forward on all PCs on an opposing side.

When you enter a chase, either in pursuit or escape, you and your adversary form separate 'sides' that both start with 0 Edge. A chase usually has two sides, the chaser(s) and the chased, but there may be more.

When you Cooperate in a chase:
• If you are not part of the chase, you must join a side of it, and are involved in that side's Edge, conclusion and consequences.
• If you are already part of the chase, you must Push Yourself to Cooperate.
When you insult, injure, or disappoint someone who Favors you, they no longer do.

When you would Favor someone you already Favor, choose one instead:

• Heal them of one condition; describe how you do so.
• Gain Advantage Forward to aid them or accomplish something for them.

When you accomplish a significant task for someone, choose two if you Favor them, or one if you don't:

• Gain 1 XP
• You no longer Favor them
• They Favor you
• You get to ask them two questions as if you Scrutinized them
When you act against someone you Favor or deny their request, roll+Nothing.

success.label: Success!
success.value:
Choose one.
• Someone else no longer Favors you, the GM will say who.
• It will cost you or come back to bite you - the GM will say how now or when it's revealed.
• You have Disadvantage Forward against them.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value:
Choose two.
• Someone else no longer Favors you, the GM will say who.
• It will cost you or come back to bite you - the GM will say how now or when it's revealed.
• You have Disadvantage Forward against them.

failure.label: Miss...
failure.value:
All three.
• Someone else no longer Favors you, the GM will say who.
• It will cost you or come back to bite you - the GM will say how now or when it's revealed.
• You have Disadvantage Forward against them.

system.description: When you call on your Follower to help you with a task, roll with Advantage, but they are also exposed to the costs or consequences of your Move. Then the GM will invoke one of their Costs, and the follower will be unwilling or unable to Assist you again until that cost is fulfilled.
When you order your Follower to do something contrary to their Costs, Want, or instincts, roll+CHA. If they Favor you, you may use up their Favor to gain Advantage on the roll.

success.label: Success!
success.value: They do it as well as you can expect.

partial.label: Partial Success
partial.value:
The GM chooses one:
• The experience endangers them - they do it but are out of the action for some time.
• They complain loudly, now or later, and demand compensation or your Favor.
• It takes them longer than expected, is done shoddily, or it will cost you later.

system.description: When your Follower does a dangerous task alone, they do it to the best of their ability, but are taken out of the action (trapped, injured, distracted, etc.). The GM will say how.
